, like smectite, are a particular type of clay that can absorb water and expand. They are part of the family of Phyllosilicates (or "sheet silicates"), a group of minerals that have a unique layered structure.
Imagine them as tiny, flat sheets stacked on top of each other like a deck of cards.

In the case of swelling clays, due to some particular asset of the layers, in contact with water, they have the ability to pull the water molecules in between their sheets, causing the entire stack to puff up or swell. The consequence is the swelling of the entire stone.
